Command: Purge Out the Old Leaven; Put Away the Wicked Person
Summary: Paul's church-purity command: purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, and put away from among yourselves that wicked person.
Commandment: Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. Therefore put away from among yourselves that wicked person.
Application: Leaven spreads through the whole lump: tolerated sin in Corinth — a man with his father's wife — corrupts the feast, which must be kept in sincerity and truth. Discipline here is purging, not vengeance, and it belongs to the church, not outsiders.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump' (1 Corinthians 5:6).
Function: A little leaven leavens the whole lump — tolerated sin in Corinth corrupted the feast. The apostles gave this one, not Moses — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal was a church kept in sincerity and truth: purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, and put away the wicked person. The evil it addressed was sin tolerated in the assembly, spreading through the whole body. It restrained that evil by discipline itself: purging belongs to the church, and it is purging, not vengeance.
